summary: HTTP Semantics (RFC 9110) defines the parts of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol that stay the same across versions: resources named by web addresses, request methods, status codes, header fields, content negotiation, conditional and partial requests, and a challenge-and-response framework for authentication. It describes an exchange of requests and responses that is stateless, with each request considered in isolation. It covers extension well, through registries and the rule that unrecognised fields can be ignored and forwarded. It leaves to others the wire encoding of each version, the cache rules, the authentication schemes themselves, and everything about the format or meaning of the content it carries. Traps for a standards audience: the status code for payment is reserved with no defined exchange, there is no way for a server to tell a client to discard cached credentials, and the step that turns a name into a reachable address depends on client-specific name resolution.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 5 Fields

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 16.3 Field Extensibility
sources.quote: Most fields are designed with the expectation that a recipient can safely ignore (but forward downstream) any field not recognized.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 16.3.1 Field Name Registry
sources.quote: The "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Field Name Registry" defines the namespace for HTTP field names.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 16.4.1 Authentication Scheme Registry
sources.quote: The "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Authentication Scheme Registry" defines the namespace for the authentication schemes in challenges and credentials.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 16.5.1 Range Unit Registry
sources.quote: The "HTTP Range Unit Registry" defines the namespace for the range unit names and refers to their corresponding specifications.

coverage.note: Searched RFC 9110 (June 2022) for revoke, revocation, suspend, status of a credential and expiry of credentials on 2026-11-03; the document says it provides no mechanism for ending cached credentials and leaves expiry and revocation to each authentication scheme.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 17.16.2 Credentials and Idle Clients
sources.quote: HTTP does not provide a mechanism for the origin server to direct clients to discard these cached credentials, since the protocol has no awareness of how credentials are obtained or managed by the user agent.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 17.16.2 Credentials and Idle Clients
sources.quote: The mechanisms for expiring or revoking credentials can be specified as part of an authentication scheme definition.

coverage.note: A client sends its preferred languages and media types with a request, but HTTP defines no store for settings or accessibility choices that follow the user between services.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 12.5.4 Accept-Language
sources.quote: The "Accept-Language" header field can be used by user agents to indicate the set of natural languages that are preferred in the response.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 12.5.1 Accept
sources.quote: The "Accept" header field can be used by user agents to specify their preferences regarding response media types.

coverage.note: Searched RFC 9110 (June 2022) for audio, streaming, voice and real-time on 2026-11-03; the only audio hit is a media-type example, and no audio streaming format or delivery rule is defined.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 3.6 Origin Server
sources.quote: Common origin servers also include home automation units, configurable networking components, office machines, autonomous robots, news feeds, traffic cameras, real-time ad selectors, and video-on-demand platforms.

coverage.note: The document and the caching document define caches for reusing responses and name content delivery networks as one cache deployment, but define no content delivery network mechanism of their own.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 3.8 Caches
sources.quote: These include national hierarchies of proxy caches to save bandwidth and reduce latency, content delivery networks that use gateway caching to optimize regional and global distribution of popular sites, collaborative systems that broadcast or multicast cache entries, archives of pre-fetched cache entries for use in off-line or high-latency environments, and so on.

sources.title: RFC 9111, HTTP Caching (June 2022), 1 Introduction
sources.quote: The goal of HTTP caching is significantly improving performance by reusing a prior response message to satisfy a current request.

coverage.note: Searched RFC 9110 (June 2022) for profile, subset, conformance level and named component on 2026-11-03; the only contract it declares is the protocol version, and no named optional subsets or levels are defined.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 2.5 Protocol Version
sources.quote: The protocol version as a whole indicates the sender's conformance with the set of requirements laid out in that version's corresponding specification(s).

coverage.note: Searched RFC 9110 (June 2022) for pairwise, unlinkable, correlation, pseudonym and anonymous on 2026-11-03; it names tracking by fingerprinting as a risk but defines no pairwise identifier or presentation mechanism.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 17.13 Browser Fingerprinting
sources.quote: Browser fingerprinting is a set of techniques for identifying a specific user agent over time through its unique set of characteristics.

coverage.note: Searched RFC 9110 (June 2022) for encrypt, recipient key and key material on 2026-11-03; it defines a secured connection for the https scheme but no recipient key material or content encryption for an intended subject.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 4.2.2 https URI Scheme
sources.quote: In this context, "secured" specifically means that the server has been authenticated as acting on behalf of the identified authority and all HTTP communication with that server has confidentiality and integrity protection that is acceptable to both client and server.

coverage.note: A whole place with its scenes, assets and behaviour is content, and HTTP defines how each resource is fetched but no file format or bundle for taking a whole world out.

sources.title: RFC 9110, HTTP Semantics (June 2022), 1.1 Purpose
sources.quote: HTTP hides the details of how a service is implemented by presenting a uniform interface to clients that is independent of the types of resources provided.
